messages:
maria_ng: Heads-up — saw a bunch of 429s show up around 11:03 UTC for org:acme while overall throughput was low. Telemetry shows we applied backpressure at the org rate limiter, but billing/usage counters jumped unexpectedly.

sam_t: Can you paste a sample request id + logs? curious if this is retry-related.

maria_ng: sure — request id `req_8a7f`:
```
2024-11-02T11:03:12Z INFO router: incoming request id=req_8a7f org=acme key=key_live_123 model=gpt-open-8k
2024-11-02T11:03:12Z INFO quota: reserve attempt reserved=0 want=120 bucket_tokens=0 backpressure=true
2024-11-02T11:03:12Z INFO worker: spawned job job=toolcall-translate subreqs=1
2024-11-02T11:03:13Z INFO worker: job complete consumed=120
2024-11-02T11:03:13Z INFO quota: charge applied charged=120
```
Notable: we see the reservation at router time as 0, backpressure flipped true, but later the worker charged 120 tokens after the tool call. That matches the billing spike.

jon_arch: Interesting — are these requests that do tool calls which expand tokens after the initial prefix? If we're only reserving prompt tokens at admission, completion/tool tokens can get billed later and bypass the admission limiter.

maria_ng: Exactly my suspicion. For this org we allow burst=200 but they hit long tail of tool completions. The router only reserves prompt tokens (est_prompt) and relies on worker to charge the completion portion. If workers apply charges post-hoc, org limits don't properly reflect peak simultaneous completions.

emily_sre: Quote from rate limiter design: "reserve at arrival for estimated total tokens including max_completion_estimate OR reject if unknown" — but we intentionally kept estimates conservative to avoid wasted reservations. Seems like the conservative estimate is too low for some tool-heavy flows.

sam_t: Two failure modes: 1) underestimated reservation -> later charge pushes org over limit (but backpressure should prevent new arrivals), 2) retries: if retry occurs and reservation wasn't durable, we might double-charge. Any evidence of duplicate charges for same id?

maria_ng: I checked — no duplicate request ids, but I did find patterns of retries from the client with different ids while the original went to worker and produced charges. So clients get 429s, retry with new id, worker still completes original toolcall and charges. Net effect = original charged + new reserved (then maybe blocked).

jon_arch: Two quick ideas: a) make reservation include `max_tool_delta` derived from model+tool mapping at router time (needs cheap heuristic), or b) change charging to provisional reservation model: atomically reserve a small completion buffer on admission and have workers reconcile on completion (refunds if unused).

emily_sre: (also) we could short-circuit: for requests that spawn tool calls, reject when bucket_tokens < (prompt + tool_min) to avoid workers running without headroom. But that hurts perf for most jobs.

sam_t: From a telemetry/billing correctness angle we should ensure meter shows both reserved and actual charged fields and correlate by trace id. Right now dashboards show charged tokens only, which hides reservations.

maria_ng: Agreed — I opened an internal eval: add fields to meter events: `reserved_at_router`, `charged_at_worker`, `reservation_id`. That will make it easier to roll up exact counts per org for a time window and compute mismatch.

jon_arch: Implementation notes: router currently uses `reserve_token_bucket(org_id, estimate)` sync path. We could extend reserve call to accept `provisional=true` and create a reservation record that worker consumes. Reservation lifetime TTL 30s, worker consumes or releases. That avoids post-hoc charges bypassing limiter.

emily_sre: Watch out for increased state and potential leak on crash. TTL+periodic sweep needed. Also consider idempotency: workers should only consume once per reservation_id to avoid double charges on retries.

maria_ng: I'll prototype a minimal change: 1) router adds provisional reservation when toolcall flag present, 2) worker consumes reservation by id before running tool, 3) if reservation exhausted, worker fails fast and returns 429 so clients can back off.

sam_t: Nice. Can you add a short design doc in eng-platform/triage with perf impact estimates? Also add a dashboard panel: "reservation vs charged delta by org" and an alert when delta > 10% for 5m.

maria_ng: Will do. Quick note: quota-bot reports a lot of 429s for acme during the window — dropping into thread.

quota-bot: org=acme alert: 60 429s in 5m (org_rate_limiter). See /dash/org/acme/ratelimit

jon_arch: Cool. If the prototype looks good we should ship to canary orgs and measure false-reject rate. Also add a unit test to catch double-charge path where worker consumes twice.

maria_ng: Thanks all — I'll post the design here once it's up. :thumbsup:
